coverage.notes: SEL: the Pennsylvania Career Ready Skills (final July 2018) are PDE's SEL learning progressions, Pre-K-12, in three domains; PDE presents them as guidance and a target for instruction, aligned with (not duplicating) the Career Education and Work Standards, and credits CASEL. Reviewer: decide whether 'guidance_only' is the more accurate status. Portrait of a Graduate: no statewide portrait was found on the PDE pages checked, and vendor pages that claim one could not be traced to a state document, so the status stays 'unknown' (absence not proven); many PA districts have their own portraits.

frameworks.name: Pennsylvania Career Ready Skills
frameworks.notes: Read from PDE's Career Ready Skills page, the one-page 'Career Ready Skills' PDF and 'The Pennsylvania Career Ready Skills Continuum' PDF (grade bands Pre-K-K, 1-5, 6-8, 9-12). Items are the three domains; the continuum PDF holds the grade-banded skills under each. Summaries paraphrase PDE's domain descriptions.

items.title: Self-Awareness and Self-Management
items.summary: Recognize and regulate emotions and thoughts: manage stress, control impulses, motivate oneself, and set and work toward personal and academic goals.

items.title: Establishing and Maintaining Relationships
items.summary: Build and keep healthy relationships with diverse people: communicate, listen, cooperate, resist inappropriate pressure, resolve conflict, and ask for or offer help.

items.title: Social Problem-Solving Skills
items.summary: Show empathy and understand others' perspectives, and make constructive, respectful choices that weigh the consequences for oneself and others.

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Calm Is A Super Power" (middle school, series: Emotional Strength). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that calm is strength under control. They will learn to identify situations that may trigger quick reactions, practice habits that support self-control, and recognize how calm responses can improve decisions, relationships, and daily ..." The lesson teaches spotting triggers and practising habits that interrupt impulsive reactions, matching the self-regulation skill.

target.title: Calm Is A Super Power - Lesson Plan 8 - 31 - #116 - MS

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Pause Before You Escalate" (middle school, series: Conflict & Self-Government). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that a conflict is escalating, practice a short pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful response that helps move the situation toward an answer." Teaches a short pause-and-reset routine before responding, matching the skill of managing emotions and behaviour.

target.title: Pause Before You Escalate - Lesson Plan 10 - 19 - #151 - MS

alignments.rationale: Tune Your Brain game "Calm Down Corner" (tagged self-management). FNE's catalog description: "Listen to a frustrating moment, then pick what would help you feel calm." Students pick what would help them calm down after a frustrating moment, which practises the same strategy-choosing skill.

FNE lesson "Stay in Control of Your Spirit" (middle school, series: Conflict & Self-Government). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that emotions are beginning to take control, practice a simple pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful action that keeps their response aligned with their values." The lesson has students recognise when emotions start driving behaviour and choose a response, which is the same skill.

target.title: Stay in Control of Your Spirit - Lesson Plan 10 - 23 - #155 - MS

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Growth Requires Repetition" (middle school, series: Personal Growth in Action). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will explain why repetition supports growth, identify one skill or habit they want to strengthen, recognize how tracking and feedback improve practice, and choose one repeated action that supports progress." Students choose a skill to strengthen, track it and adjust with feedback, which is goal-setting and monitoring. Limit: Goals are personal habits; it does not cover career or post-graduation planning.

target.title: Growth Requires Repetition - Lesson Plan 9 - 21 - #131 - MS

alignments.rationale: Morning Boost program theme "Emotional Intelligence" (programs.html). FNE's published description: "Understanding and naming emotions, managing reactions, building empathy, and developing the self-awareness that underlies every other social-emotional skill." The theme names managing reactions and self-awareness. Program-level: shows the theme is part of the offering, not which lesson teaches it. Limit: The PA domain also covers goal-setting toward post-secondary and career plans, which FNE addresses only at the habit level.

FNE lesson "Say What You Mean With Respect" (middle school, series: Communication That Helps). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that respectful communication means being honest, clear, and kind at the same time. They will learn to pause before reacting, explain without blaming, choose helpful words, and speak in a way that builds understanding instead of ..." Teaches clear, honest, kind speaking and explaining without blame.

target.title: Say What You Mean With Respect - Lesson Plan: 6 - 8 - #56_MS

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Listen Before You Answer" (middle school, series: Respect & Character). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that strong communication is not only about what they say. It is also about how well they listen. Students will learn to pause before answering, let others finish speaking, ask respectful questions, and respond with care, wisdom, and ..." Teaches letting others finish, asking respectful questions and responding with care, which is the listening half of the skill.

target.title: Listen Before You Answer - Lesson Plan: 6 - 3 - #53_MS

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Ask for Help the Right Way" (middle school, series: Communication That Helps). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that needing help does not mean they are weak. It means they are honest enough to recognize when they need support. Students will learn to ask clearly, speak respectfully, listen carefully, and keep trying instead of shutting down or ..." Teaches asking clearly and respectfully and keeping going rather than shutting down, which includes seeking help.

target.title: Ask for Help the Right Way - Lesson Plan: 6 - 9 - #57_MS

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Pause Before You Escalate" (middle school, series: Conflict & Self-Government). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that a conflict is escalating, practice a short pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful response that helps move the situation toward an answer." Students spot the signs a conflict is escalating and choose a respectful response that moves toward an answer.

target.title: Pause Before You Escalate - Lesson Plan 10 - 19 - #151 - MS

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Choose Peace Without Losing Strength" (middle school, series: Conflict & Self-Government). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will distinguish peace from passivity, identify one calm and assertive response to conflict, and explain when respectful help-seeking protects safety, boundaries, or a fair solution." Students practise a calm, assertive response to conflict and learn when respectful help-seeking protects a fair solution.

target.title: Choose Peace Without Losing Strength - Lesson Plan 10 - 20 - #152 - MS

alignments.rationale: Morning Boost program theme "Communication & Relationships" (programs.html). FNE's published description: "Developing skills for active listening, expressing yourself clearly, navigating conflict, and building healthy relationships - inside and outside the classroom." The theme names listening, expressing yourself clearly, conflict and healthy relationships. Program-level: shows the theme is part of the offering, not which lesson teaches it. Limit: The PA domain also stresses diversity; FNE content here is about respect in general.

FNE lesson "Think Past the Moment" (middle school, series: Decision Making & Consequences). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify an immediate result and a possible later consequence of a choice, explain who else may be affected, and choose one caring, responsible action." Students identify an immediate and a later consequence, who else is affected, and choose a caring action.

target.title: Think Past the Moment - Lesson Plan 10 - 5 - #141 - MS

alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Think Before You Act" (middle school, series: Self-Control & Daily Choices). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that wise choices often begin with a pause. They will learn that self-control means slowing down long enough to think clearly, notice consequences, manage pressure, and choose what is right instead of reacting too quickly." Teaches pausing to notice consequences and manage pressure before choosing.

target.title: Think Before You Act - Lesson Plan 7 - 6 - #76_MS

alignments.rationale: Tune Your Brain game "Sharing Circle" (tagged social awareness and relationship skills). FNE's catalog description: "Listen to what happened, then pick the kind thing to do." Students listen to what happened to someone and choose the kind response, which practises noticing another person's experience. Limit: Everyday kindness scenarios; does not teach perspective-taking across cultures or backgrounds.

Tune Your Brain game "Decision Point" (tagged social awareness, relationship skills and responsible decision-making). FNE's catalog description: "Work through a real Issues-to-Answers cycle on a peer situation - recognize, understand impact, consider options, choose, and reflect." The cycle includes understanding the impact of a situation on others before choosing.

Morning Boost program theme "Healthy Decisions" (programs.html). FNE's published description: "Applying the Issues-to-Answers framework to real-life decisions involving peer pressure, risk, choices, and consequences." The theme names choices and consequences. Program-level: shows the theme is part of the offering, not which lesson teaches it. Limit: PA's domain also names understanding others' backgrounds; FNE covers kindness and impact on others, not cultural perspective-taking.
